standing order = an instruction to send a fixed sum from your account on set dates
bank transfer = sending money from one account to another electronically
chip and PIN = paying by putting a card in a machine and typing a secret number
digital wallet = an app that stores card details so you can pay with a phone
invoice = a document that lists goods or services and the money owed
VAT = a tax added to the price of many goods and services
proof of purchase = a receipt or document that shows you bought something
transaction = an act of buying, selling or moving money
bank statement = a list of money going in and out of your account
overdrawn = having spent more than is in your bank account
in the red = owing money to the bank; having a negative balance
in the black = having money left; not owing the bank
debt = money that you owe to a person or a bank
run up a debt = to gradually owe more and more money
pay off = to finish paying all the money you owe
exchange rate = how much one currency is worth in another
exchange commission = a fee charged for changing one currency into another
cashpoint = a machine in a wall that gives you cash from your account
building society = a financial organisation that offers savings accounts and mortgages
lump sum = an amount of money paid all at once, not in parts
